members: Methadone (Full μ-agonist, NMDA antagonist, SNRI) (StahlNeuro p.559)
Buprenorphine (Partial μ-agonist, κ-antagonist, ceiling effect) (StahlNeuro p.559)
Naloxone (Pure full μ-antagonist, rapid displacement) (StahlNeuro p.560)
drug_class.mechanism: Gi-coupled μ-opioid receptor activation or blockade altering cAMP and VSCC channels, modulating mesolimbic dopamine release (StahlNeuro p.31, 541, 559)
kinetics: Methadone t½ = 24–36 hours (DSM p.618, StahlNeuro p.560)
Naloxone short t½ = 30–90 minutes (DSM p.616, StahlNeuro p.560)
Sublocade SC depot lasts 30 days (StahlNeuro p.559–560)
Vivitrol IM depot lasts 30 days (StahlNeuro p.562)
drug_class.onset_of_effect: Naloxone IN/IM acts in minutes; SL Buprenorphine acts in 15–30 min; Methadone steady state in 3–5 days (StahlNeuro p.559–560, DSM p.616)

items: Methadone: OUD maintenance & detoxification for ages 16+ (Dulcan p.234, DSM p.610)
Buprenorphine: Office-based MAT maintenance & detoxification for ages 16+ (Dulcan p.234, StahlNeuro p.559)
Naltrexone (Vivitrol): OUD relapse prevention for ages 18+ after 7–10 days opioid-free (Dulcan p.234, StahlNeuro p.560)
Naloxone: Emergency opioid overdose reversal without age limit (DSM p.616, StahlNeuro p.560)
Clonidine/Lofexidine: Symptomatic relief of autonomic opioid withdrawal symptoms (StahlKids p.143, StahlNeuro p.560)
key_numbers: 16 years — FDA minimum age for Methadone and Buprenorphine MAT (Dulcan p.234)
18 years — FDA minimum age for Vivitrol (XR-NTX) (Dulcan p.234)
7–10 days — Mandatory opioid-free interval before starting Naltrexone (Dulcan p.234–235)

items: Methadone: QTc prolongation, Torsades de Pointes, respiratory depression, constipation, diaphoresis (Dulcan p.234, 332, StahlNeuro p.559)
Buprenorphine: Precipitated withdrawal if given prematurely with full agonists, headache, nausea (DSM p.618, StahlNeuro p.559)
Naltrexone: Severe precipitated withdrawal if given early, fatal overdose risk upon relapse due to receptor up-regulation, hepatotoxicity (StahlKids p.144, StahlNeuro p.560)
Naloxone: Acute precipitated withdrawal, agitation, tachycardia, rare pulmonary edema (DSM p.616, StahlNeuro p.560)
Clonidine: Hypotension, bradycardia, sedation, rebound hypertension if stopped abruptly (StahlKids p.143–144)
key_numbers: 440 ms — QTc upper limit threshold on ECG requiring cardiology review for Methadone (Dulcan p.1095)
3–5 times ULN — Transaminase elevation limit for stopping Naltrexone/Buprenorphine (StahlNeuro p.560)

items: Methadone: Baseline & follow-up ECG for QTc interval, specialized UDS (Dulcan p.234, 332, DSM p.612)
Buprenorphine: COWS score (>8–12) before induction, baseline & periodic LFTs, specialized UDS (DSM p.612, 618, StahlNeuro p.560)
Naltrexone: LFTs, verification of 7–10 days opioid-free status or Naloxone challenge test (Dulcan p.234, StahlNeuro p.560, DSM p.616)
Naloxone: Vital signs & respiratory rate monitoring for 2–4 hours post-administration (DSM p.616, StahlNeuro p.560)
Clonidine: BP and pulse before each dose (StahlKids p.143–144)
key_numbers: 8–12 points — COWS minimum active withdrawal score required before Buprenorphine induction (DSM p.618, StahlNeuro p.559)
2–4 hours — Mandatory observation window post-Naloxone for Renarcotization risk (DSM p.616, StahlNeuro p.560)
90/60 mmHg — BP cutoff below which Clonidine doses must be held (StahlKids p.143–144)

items: Methadone: OTP clinic-only daily directly observed therapy (DOT); starting dose 20–30 mg/day, maintenance 60–120 mg/day (Dulcan p.234, StahlNeuro p.559)
Buprenorphine (Suboxone): Office-based SL formulation with 4:1 Naloxone ratio to deter IV abuse; maintenance 8–16 mg/day (max 24 mg/day) (Dulcan p.234–235, StahlNeuro p.559)
Naltrexone (Vivitrol): Monthly 380 mg IM gluteal injection after 7–10 days opioid-free; produces pharmacological extinction (Dulcan p.234–235, StahlNeuro p.560, 562)
Naloxone: IN spray 4 mg (Narcan) or IM 0.4–2 mg; repeat every 2–3 min if needed; call emergency transport immediately (DSM p.616, StahlNeuro p.560)
Clonidine: Oral 0.1 mg tid for 4–6 days; limit outpatient supply to 3 days maximum (StahlKids p.143–144)
key_numbers: 4:1 ratio — Buprenorphine to Naloxone in Suboxone SL tablets/films (Dulcan p.234, StahlNeuro p.559)
380 mg — Monthly IM dose of Extended-Release Naltrexone (Vivitrol) (StahlNeuro p.562, Dulcan p.235)
4 mg — Single-dose IN Naloxone spray (Narcan) for emergency overdose (StahlNeuro p.560)
3 days — Maximum outpatient Clonidine supply limit for detox (StahlKids p.144)

high_yield: DSM-5-TR Diagnostic Exception: Tolerance and withdrawal criteria do NOT count towards OUD when opioids are taken under proper medical supervision (DSM p.609, 610).
FDA Age Approvals: Buprenorphine (16+), Methadone (16+), Vivitrol (18+) (Dulcan p.234).
Methadone QTc Risk: Methadone prolongs QTc interval and increases Torsades de Pointes risk; requires baseline and follow-up ECGs (Dulcan p.234, 332).

Buprenorphine Precipitated Withdrawal: Administering Buprenorphine prematurely displaces full agonists and triggers severe withdrawal; requires active withdrawal (COWS > 8–12) before induction (DSM p.618, StahlNeuro p.559).
Suboxone Abuse Deterrence: Naloxone component is unabsorbed sublingually (~0% bioavailability) but causes severe withdrawal if dissolved and injected IV (Dulcan p.234–235, StahlNeuro p.559).

Naltrexone Opioid-Free Requirement: Requires 7–10 days opioid-free status (10–14 days for long-acting) before starting; relapse after stopping carries high risk of fatal overdose due to loss of tolerance and receptor up-regulation (Dulcan p.234–235, StahlNeuro p.560).

Naloxone Short Half-Life & Renarcotization: Naloxone t½ (30–90 min) is shorter than most opioids; patient can relapse into coma (Renarcotization), requiring mandatory hospital transport and potential re-dosing (DSM p.616, StahlNeuro p.560).
Toxicology Screen Limits: Routine UDS detects morphine only; Fentanyl, Methadone, Buprenorphine, and Oxycodone require specialized toxicology panels (DSM p.612).
